source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client says he feels his amputated foot cramping. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Phantom limb pain is real; acknowledge it, keep active, use distraction and desensitization.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amputation Nursing (PDF p. 458)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: To prevent hip flexion contracture after above-knee amputation, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Prone positioning prevents flexion contracture; avoid pillows under stump and abduction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amputation Nursing (PDF p. 458)
questions.quote: Turn side to side Assume prone position

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is the residual limb wrapped with an elastic bandage?
questions.rationale: Compression controls edema and shapes the stump for prosthesis fit.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amputation Nursing (PDF p. 458)
questions.quote: The residual limb must be shaped into a conical form

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which item should be at the bedside of a client after amputation?
questions.rationale: A tourniquet in plain sight is needed for massive hemorrhage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amputation Complications (PDF p. 459)
questions.quote: A large tourniquet should be in plain sight at the patients bedside

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During passive ROM, a spastic muscle resists movement. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Stop temporarily, apply slow gentle pressure until relaxation, then continue.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Passive ROM (PDF p. 459)
questions.quote: If muscle spasticity occurs, stop temporarily

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with left leg weakness uses a cane. Which hand holds the cane?
questions.rationale: Hold the cane on the stronger side; move cane with weak leg.
questions.quote: Hold the cane with the hand on the stronger side of the body

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Crutch users should bear weight on the:
questions.rationale: Axillary pressure can injure the radial nerve (crutch palsy).
questions.quote: The weight should be borne by the arms rather than the axillae

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Properly fitted axillary crutches leave a gap below the axilla of about:
questions.rationale: Shoulder rest 2.5–5 cm (2–3 finger widths) below axilla; elbow flexed about 30 degrees.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Measuring Crutches (PDF p. 460)
questions.quote: 2.5 to 5 cm (1 to 2 in) below the axilla

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which crutch gait is safest, keeping three points of support?
questions.rationale: Four-point is most elementary and safest; requires weight bearing on both legs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Crutch Gaits (PDF p. 460)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client who cannot bear weight on one leg should use which gait?
questions.rationale: Three-point: both crutches and weak leg advance, then the strong leg.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Crutch Gaits (PDF p. 460)
questions.quote: The two crutches and the unaffected leg bear weight alternately

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Going up stairs on crutches, the client first moves the:
questions.rationale: Up with the good, down with the bad; affected leg always supported by crutches.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Crutches on Stairs (PDF p. 461)
questions.quote: move the unaffected leg onto the step

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which teaching helps a client with acute low back pain?
questions.rationale: Avoid twisting, bending, lifting; limit sitting; firm mattress; short bed rest.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Low Back Pain (PDF p. 461)
questions.quote: Avoid twisting, Bending, lifting, and reaching

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Tingling when the nurse taps over the median nerve at the wrist is:
questions.rationale: Tinel's sign suggests carpal tunnel; Phalen's uses forced wrist flexion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Carpal Tunnel (PDF p. 462)
questions.quote: Tinel's sign may be elicited in patients with carpal tunnel syndrome

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Carpal tunnel syndrome involves compression of the:
questions.rationale: Median nerve entrapment from repetitive wrist movement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Carpal Tunnel (PDF p. 462)
questions.quote: median nerve at the wrist is compressed

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Progressive contracture of the palmar fascia flexing the ring and little fingers is:
questions.rationale: Dupuytren's: palmar fascia contracture, common in men over 50.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dupuytren's Disease (PDF p. 463)
questions.quote: Slowly progressive contracture of the palmar fascia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a risk factor for osteoporosis?
questions.rationale: Risks: postmenopausal women, Asian, sedentary, corticosteroids, carbonated drinks.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.rationale: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry; plain x-ray misses early loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteoporosis Diagnosis (PDF p. 464)
questions.quote: Osteoporosis is diagnosed by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which exercise best helps prevent osteoporosis?
questions.rationale: Weight-bearing exercise like walking promotes bone formation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteoporosis Treatment (PDF p. 464)
questions.quote: Regular weight-bearing exercise promotes bone formation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Osteomalacia is primarily caused by deficiency of:
questions.rationale: Lack of calcitriol impairs calcium absorption and bone mineralization.
